nodejs: In a Node.js CommonJS script, what is printed by: setTimeout(() => console.log('A'), 0); Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log('B')); console.log('C');
C, B, A
A, B, C
C, A, B
B, C, A
Synchronous code runs first, then the microtask queue (the promise callback), and only then the timers phase of the event loop runs the setTimeout callback.
In a Node.js CommonJS script, what is printed by: Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log('promise')); process.nextTick(() => console.log('tick'));
tick, then promise
promise, then tick
Only tick is printed
The order is random on each run
Node.js drains the process.nextTick queue before the promise microtask queue, so tick is printed first even though it was scheduled second.
Inside an fs.readFile callback you call setTimeout(cb1, 0) and setImmediate(cb2). Which runs first in Node.js?
cb2, because the check phase follows the poll phase
cb1, because timers always run before anything else
The order is unpredictable inside I/O callbacks
Both run at the same time on different threads
I/O callbacks run in the poll phase; the next phase is check (setImmediate), and timers only run on the following loop iteration, so cb2 is guaranteed to run first.
Which phase of the Node.js event loop executes setImmediate() callbacks?
The check phase
The timers phase
The close callbacks phase
The pending callbacks phase
setImmediate callbacks are queued for the check phase, which runs right after the poll phase.
What does it mean that Node.js uses non-blocking I/O?
The main thread starts an I/O operation and keeps running other code until a callback reports the result
Each incoming request is handled by its own dedicated operating system thread
I/O calls run on the main thread but are given a higher priority
JavaScript code is paused while the disk or network is busy
Node.js delegates I/O to the OS or libuv and continues executing; results come back later as events processed by the event loop.
Which of these Node.js operations is executed on the libuv thread pool?
crypto.pbkdf2()
setTimeout()
process.nextTick()
Promise.resolve()
File system operations, dns.lookup, some crypto functions such as pbkdf2, and zlib use the libuv thread pool. Timers and microtasks are handled on the main thread.
Which environment variable changes the size of the libuv thread pool used by Node.js (default 4)?
UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE
NODE_THREADPOOL_SIZE
LIBUV_MAX_THREADS
NODE_WORKER_COUNT
libuv reads UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE when the pool is first used; it must be set before the pool starts, usually in the environment.
An Express route on Node.js runs a CPU-heavy synchronous loop for 5 seconds. What happens to other incoming requests during those 5 seconds?
They wait, because the event loop is blocked
They are served by another thread automatically
They are rejected with HTTP 503 by Node.js
They run in parallel thanks to non-blocking I/O
JavaScript runs on a single main thread. Synchronous CPU work blocks the event loop, so no other callbacks or requests are processed until it finishes.
In Node.js, what does Buffer.from('café').length return?
Buffer.from uses UTF-8 by default. The letters c, a and f take one byte each, and é takes two bytes, so the buffer is 5 bytes long while the string has 4 characters.
What is the key difference between Buffer.alloc(10) and Buffer.allocUnsafe(10) in Node.js?
allocUnsafe does not zero-fill memory, so it may contain old data
allocUnsafe creates a buffer that cannot be resized later
alloc returns a Promise while allocUnsafe is synchronous
allocUnsafe skips bounds checking when writing bytes
Buffer.alloc fills the memory with zeros. allocUnsafe is faster but returns uninitialized memory, so it must be fully overwritten before being exposed.
Which Node.js stream type should you implement to compress data as it flows through, like zlib.createGzip() does?
Transform
Readable
Writable
PassThrough
A Transform stream is a Duplex stream whose output is computed from its input. PassThrough is a Transform that does not change the data at all.
In Node.js, writable.write(chunk) returns false. What should well-behaved code do?
Stop writing until the stream emits 'drain'
Retry the same chunk immediately in a loop
Call writable.end() because the stream failed
Ignore it, the return value is informational only
A false return means the internal buffer is above highWaterMark. Waiting for 'drain' is how backpressure is respected and memory use stays bounded.
Why is stream.pipeline() preferred over chaining a.pipe(b).pipe(c) in Node.js?
It forwards errors and destroys all streams on failure
It is the only way to connect more than two streams
It converts all streams to object mode
It runs each stream on a separate worker thread
.pipe() does not propagate errors between streams, which can leak file descriptors. pipeline() handles errors and cleanup and accepts a final callback or returns a promise.
What happens when a Node.js EventEmitter emits an 'error' event and no 'error' listener is registered?
The error is thrown, which crashes the process if uncaught
The event is silently ignored
The error is logged and execution continues
The emitter retries the event once
'error' is special: without a listener, emit('error') throws the error. Always attach an 'error' listener to emitters such as streams and sockets.
In Node.js, what is printed by: const e = new EventEmitter(); e.once('x', () => console.log('hi')); e.emit('x'); e.emit('x');
hi once
hi twice
Nothing
An error on the second emit
A listener added with once() is removed right before it is invoked the first time, so the second emit has no listeners.
In Node.js, what is printed by: e.on('a', () => console.log(1)); e.emit('a'); console.log(2); where e is an EventEmitter?
1, then 2
2, then 1
Only 2
1 and 2 in random order
EventEmitter.emit() calls listeners synchronously in the order they were registered, so the listener runs before the next line.
Your Node.js service must resize images (CPU-heavy) without blocking request handling. Which built-in module fits best?
worker_threads
cluster with one process
events
async_hooks
worker_threads runs JavaScript in parallel threads, keeping the main event loop free. async_hooks only tracks async resources and does not add parallelism.
Two Node.js worker threads need to read and write the same memory without copying it. What should they use?
A SharedArrayBuffer passed via postMessage
A regular object passed via postMessage
A global variable defined in the main thread
A JSON string sent with process.send()
postMessage normally clones data, so each side gets its own copy. A SharedArrayBuffer is shared, and Atomics can coordinate access to it.
Inside a Node.js ES module (.mjs file), which identifier is NOT defined by default?
__dirname
import.meta
globalThis
process
CommonJS wrapper variables such as __dirname, __filename and require do not exist in ESM. Use import.meta.url, or import.meta.dirname in recent Node.js versions.
A Node.js ES module runs: import pkg from './legacy.cjs'; where legacy.cjs sets module.exports = { a: 1 }. What is pkg?
The object { a: 1 }
undefined
A Promise resolving to { a: 1 }
An object { default: { a: 1 } } nested twice
When ESM imports CommonJS, the default export is the value of module.exports, so pkg is { a: 1 }.
express: How does Express recognize a middleware function as error-handling middleware?
It has four parameters: (err, req, res, next)
It is registered with app.error() instead of app.use()
Its name starts with the word error
It returns a rejected Promise
Express checks the function's arity. Only functions with exactly four parameters are treated as error handlers, so keep next even if unused.
An Express middleware neither sends a response nor calls next(). What does the client experience?
The request hangs until it times out
Express sends 404 automatically
Express sends an empty 200 response
The next middleware runs anyway
Express only moves forward when next() is called. If the response is never ended, the connection stays open until a client or server timeout.
An Express POST route reads req.body.name, but req.body is undefined even though the client sends JSON with Content-Type application/json. What is the most likely fix?
Register app.use(express.json()) before the route
Read the body from req.params instead
Add res.json() at the start of the handler
Change the route from app.post to app.all
Express does not parse bodies by default. express.json() populates req.body, and it must be registered before the routes that need it.
In Express, a route is defined as app.get('/users/:id', handler) and the request is GET /users/42. What is req.params.id?
The string '42'
The number 42
undefined
An array ['42']
Route parameters are always strings; convert them yourself, for example with Number(req.params.id).
In Express, how do you read the value of q from the request GET /search?q=node?
req.query.q
req.params.q
req.body.q
req.search.q
Query string values are parsed into req.query. req.params holds named route segments like :id.
In Express, const router = express.Router(); router.get('/users', h); app.use('/api', router); Which path reaches h?
GET /api/users
GET /users
GET /api
GET /users/api
A router mounted with app.use('/api', router) prefixes all of its routes with /api.
With app.use(express.static('public')) in Express, at which URL is the file public/css/app.css served?
/css/app.css
/public/css/app.css
/static/css/app.css
/app.css
express.static serves files relative to the given folder, and the folder name itself is not part of the URL unless you mount it under a path.
In Express, which line serves the folder public under URLs that start with /assets?
app.use('/assets', express.static('public'))
app.static('/assets', 'public')
app.get('/assets', express.static('public'))
express.static('public', '/assets')
Passing a mount path to app.use makes the static middleware handle /assets/* and map the remainder to files inside public.
An Express handler calls res.send('ok') and then res.json({ a: 1 }). What happens?
An error: headers cannot be set after they are sent
The client receives both bodies, one after the other
The JSON replaces the text response
The second call is silently ignored
Each request gets exactly one response. After res.send() ends it, the second call throws ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT.
A classic HTML form posts data as application/x-www-form-urlencoded to an Express app. Which middleware fills req.body?
express.urlencoded({ extended: true })
express.json({ strict: false })
express.text()
express.raw()
express.urlencoded parses URL-encoded form bodies. express.json only parses bodies whose content type is JSON.
An Express app must accept file uploads sent as multipart/form-data. What is the usual approach?
Use a multipart parser such as multer
Use express.json() with a larger limit
Use express.urlencoded({ extended: true })
Read the file from req.query
Express's built-in parsers do not handle multipart bodies. Libraries such as multer or busboy parse them and expose the files.
A frontend on http://localhost:5173 calls an Express API on http://localhost:3000 and the browser reports a CORS error. Where must this be fixed?
On the API, by sending Access-Control-Allow-Origin
In the frontend, by adding mode: 'no-cors' to fetch
In the browser settings of each user
On the API, by returning status 200 for errors
CORS is enforced by the browser based on the server's response headers. mode: 'no-cors' only gives an opaque response that the code cannot read.
Which browser request triggers a CORS preflight OPTIONS request to an Express API on another origin?
fetch POST with Content-Type: application/json
fetch GET with no custom headers
Form POST with application/x-www-form-urlencoded
HEAD request with no custom headers
application/json is not a CORS-safelisted content type, so the browser sends a preflight. Simple GET, HEAD and form posts skip it.
An Express API uses the cors package with origin: '*' and the frontend sends cookies with credentials: 'include'. Why does the browser block it?
Wildcard origins are not allowed with credentials
Cookies are never sent to other origins
The cors package does not support cookies
Express rejects cookies sent from other origins
For credentialed requests the server must echo the specific origin and send Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true; '*' is rejected by the browser.
In Express 4, an async route handler throws an error after an await. What happens if you do not catch it?
It becomes an unhandled rejection; error middleware never sees it
Express catches it and passes it to error-handling middleware
Express retries the handler once
Express responds with 400 Bad Request and logs it
Express 4 does not inspect promises returned by handlers. You must catch and call next(err), use a wrapper, or upgrade to Express 5, which forwards rejections.
Where should error-handling middleware be registered in an Express app?
After all routes and other middleware
Before any routes, right after app is created
Inside every route handler
In a separate Express app
Errors passed to next(err) travel forward through the stack, so error handlers must come after the routes that may produce errors.
An Express handler runs res.status(404); and nothing else. What does the client receive?
Nothing yet; the request hangs
A 404 response with an empty body
A 404 page generated by Express
A 200 response
res.status() only sets the status code and returns res for chaining. A method like res.send(), res.json() or res.end() must actually send the response.
In Express, an authentication middleware loads the current user. Which object is designed for passing it to later handlers in the same request?
res.locals
app.locals
req.params
process.env
res.locals is scoped to a single request. app.locals is shared by the entire application, so per-user data there would leak between requests.
A client posts a 2 MB JSON body to an Express route using express.json() with default options. What happens?
The request is rejected with 413 Payload Too Large
The body is silently truncated to the first 100 kB
The body is parsed normally
req.body is set to an empty object
express.json() has a default limit of 100kb. Larger bodies produce a 413 error unless you raise the limit option.
A logging middleware is registered with app.use() after all routes in Express. Why does it never log successful requests?
Routes that send a response do not call next()
Middleware registered after routes is ignored
app.use() only runs for errors
Logging requires app.all() instead
Express runs the stack in registration order. Once a route ends the response without calling next(), later middleware is never reached.
nestjs: In NestJS, a class decorated with @Controller('cats') has a method decorated with @Get(':id'). Which request does it handle?
The controller prefix and the method path are combined, and @Get restricts the handler to GET requests.
In a NestJS controller, how do you read the id route parameter of GET /users/:id?
@Param extracts route parameters. @Query reads the query string, and @Body reads the request body.
In a NestJS controller, which decorator gives a handler access to the parsed request body?
@Body() injects the request body, optionally a single property like @Body('name'), and is commonly typed with a DTO class.
What HTTP status code does a NestJS @Post() handler return by default on success?
Nest returns 201 for POST and 200 for other methods by default. Use @HttpCode() to change it.
What does the @Injectable() decorator do for a NestJS class?
Marks it as a provider that the DI container can manage
Registers it as an HTTP route handler
Makes it a global module automatically
Turns it into a request-scoped singleton
@Injectable() attaches metadata so Nest can instantiate the class and inject it where needed, after it is listed in a module's providers.
What is the default scope of a NestJS provider?
Singleton, shared across the whole application
A new instance per module import
By default providers are singletons. Scope.REQUEST or Scope.TRANSIENT can be set explicitly when needed.
NestJS throws: Nest can't resolve dependencies of the OrdersService (?). UsersService lives in UsersModule. What is the usual fix?
Export UsersService from UsersModule and import UsersModule in OrdersModule
Call new UsersService() inside the constructor
A provider is private to its module unless exported. The consuming module must import the module that exports it.
In NestJS, a module has providers: [{ provide: 'CONFIG', useValue: { port: 3000 } }]. How do you inject it into a service constructor?
String or symbol tokens cannot be resolved from the type alone, so @Inject(token) tells Nest which provider to use.
Which NestJS provider definition creates a value by running a function that receives other providers?
useFactory lets you build a provider dynamically, and the inject array lists the tokens Nest passes as arguments to the factory.
Two NestJS services inject each other and Nest reports a circular dependency. Which built-in helper resolves it?
forwardRef defers resolution of the referenced class. It should be used on both sides, and it is often better to refactor the shared logic out.
A NestJS handler uses @Param('id', ParseIntPipe) id: number. What happens for the request GET /items/abc?
id becomes NaN and the handler runs
id becomes 0 and the handler runs
ParseIntPipe throws a BadRequestException when the value is not a numeric string, so the handler never runs.
In a NestJS app, ValidationPipe is configured with whitelist: true. What happens to body properties that have no class-validator decorator in the DTO?
They are stripped from the validated object
whitelist: true removes non-decorated properties. Adding forbidNonWhitelisted: true makes them produce an error instead.
What does transform: true do in NestJS's ValidationPipe?
Converts payloads into DTO class instances and primitive types
Converts the response body to JSON
With transform enabled, the plain body becomes an instance of the DTO class, and params declared as number can be converted from strings.
In a NestJS DTO using class-validator, which decorators ensure age is an integer of at least 18?
@Min checks a numeric minimum. @MinLength and @Length validate string length, not numeric value.
Why does NestJS recommend defining DTOs as classes rather than TypeScript interfaces?
Interfaces are erased at runtime, so pipes cannot use them
Interfaces cannot be exported from modules
ValidationPipe relies on runtime metadata from classes and their decorators. Interfaces disappear after compilation.
Which method must a NestJS interceptor implement, and what does it call to run the route handler?
next.handle() returns an RxJS Observable of the handler's result, so interceptors can map, time or cache the response.
For one incoming request in NestJS, in which order do these run before the route handler?
The request lifecycle is middleware, guards, interceptors (before), pipes, then the handler, followed by interceptors (after) and exception filters.
A NestJS guard's canActivate() returns false. What does the client receive by default?
Nest throws a ForbiddenException when a guard denies access. Throw UnauthorizedException yourself if you want 401.
In NestJS, a custom @Roles('admin') decorator sets metadata on a handler. What does a RolesGuard typically use to read it?
Reflector reads metadata attached with SetMetadata or Reflector.createDecorator, using the handler and class from the ExecutionContext.
How is a JWT strategy from @nestjs/passport usually applied to a NestJS route?
Authentication in Nest is implemented with guards. AuthGuard('jwt') runs the registered Passport JWT strategy before the handler.
deno: A script started with deno run main.ts (no permission flags) calls fetch('https://example.com'). What happens?
Network access is denied unless the user grants it
The request succeeds, since fetch is a web standard
Deno downgrades the request to plain HTTP
The request succeeds but its body is empty
Deno is secure by default: network, file, env and subprocess access require permission, granted by a flag or, in an interactive terminal, by answering a prompt.
Which deno run flag lets a script make network requests only to api.example.com?
Most Deno permission flags accept an allow-list, so --allow-net=api.example.com grants access to that host and nothing else.
A Deno script should read files only inside the ./data folder. Which flag fits best?
--allow-read with a path limits read access to that path. Plain --allow-read grants read access to the whole file system.
In Deno, what does the -A flag of deno run do?
-A is short for --allow-all. It is convenient locally but removes Deno's sandbox, so prefer specific flags in production.
A Deno script runs Deno.env.get('API_KEY'). Which permission does it need?
Reading environment variables is guarded by the env permission, which can also be scoped, for example --allow-env=API_KEY.
A Deno script uses new Deno.Command('git', { args: ['status'] }) to start a subprocess. Which permission does it need?
Spawning subprocesses requires the run permission, which can be limited to specific programs, such as --allow-run=git.
How can Deno code check at runtime whether it has network permission?
Deno.permissions.query returns a PermissionStatus whose state is 'granted', 'prompt' or 'denied'. Deno.permissions.request can ask for it.
How do you run a TypeScript file main.ts with Deno?
Compile with tsc, then run deno run main.js
deno compile main.ts, then run the .js output
Deno executes TypeScript directly without a separate build step or extra configuration.
In Deno 2, does deno run main.ts type-check the code by default?
No; it skips type checking unless you use deno check or --check
Yes, and it refuses to run on any type error
Yes, but it only reports warnings
No; Deno strips TypeScript and has no type checker
Since Deno 1.23, deno run only transpiles. Use deno check main.ts or deno run --check to get full type checking.
What is the name of Deno's project configuration file, where tasks, imports and compiler options are set?
deno.json (or deno.jsonc) holds tasks, the import map, compilerOptions, lint and fmt settings.
In Deno, Deno.serve((req) => handler(req)) is used to build an HTTP server. What should the handler return?
A Response object, or a Promise of one
A plain string with the body
An object with status and body fields
Deno.serve is built on web standards: the handler receives a Request and returns a Response, just like a fetch event in a browser service worker.
Without a port option, on which port does Deno.serve(handler) listen?
Deno.serve defaults to port 8000 on all interfaces; pass { port } to change it.
Which global API is available in Deno for hashing data without importing any module?
Deno implements the Web Crypto API as a global. require is not available in native Deno modules.
As of Deno 2, where is the official Deno standard library (such as @std/path) published?
On the JSR registry under the @std scope
On GitHub releases as zip files
The standard library moved to JSR, so you import it like jsr:@std/path or add it with deno add jsr:@std/path.
Which import is the usual way to write assertions for Deno.test with the standard library?
@std/assert provides assertEquals, assertThrows and more. Tests are declared with Deno.test and run with deno test.
How does a Deno 2 project import the Express package?
It cannot, since Deno has no npm support
The npm: specifier lets Deno use npm packages directly, and Deno 2 also understands package.json and node_modules.
Which Deno command produces a standalone executable that runs without Deno installed?
deno compile embeds the runtime and your code into a single binary, keeping the permission flags you pass at compile time.
Which Deno API loads a native shared library (.so, .dylib or .dll) through the foreign function interface?
Deno.dlopen takes the library path and a map of symbol definitions, and returns an object whose symbols can be called from JavaScript.
Which permission flag does a Deno program need to call Deno.dlopen()?
Loading native code bypasses the sandbox, so FFI has its own permission. Treat --allow-ffi as nearly equivalent to full access.
In Deno, const lib = Deno.dlopen('./libmath.so', { add: { parameters: ['i32', 'i32'], result: 'i32' } }); How do you call add?
Functions declared in the symbol map are exposed on lib.symbols. Call lib.close() when the library is no longer needed.
bun: Which JavaScript engine does Bun use?
Bun is built on JavaScriptCore, the engine from WebKit. Node.js and Deno use V8.
Bun's JavaScript engine is the same engine used by which browser?
JavaScriptCore is developed as part of WebKit, which powers Safari.
In which programming language is most of Bun's runtime written?
Bun is written mainly in Zig, plus C++ for the JavaScriptCore bindings. Deno, by comparison, is written in Rust.
When Bun runs a .ts file directly with bun index.ts, what happens to type errors?
They are not reported; Bun transpiles without type checking
Bun refuses to run the file
Bun prints them as warnings and continues
Bun strips types and executes the code. Run tsc --noEmit separately, for example in CI, to catch type errors.
Which import gives you test and expect in Bun's built-in test runner?
bun:test is Bun's Jest-compatible test module, and bun test runs the matching test files.
Which file does bun test pick up automatically?
bun test looks for files whose names contain .test or .spec (or _test, _spec) with a JavaScript or TypeScript extension.
Which command bundles ./src/index.ts with Bun's native bundler into the ./dist folder?
bun build is the CLI for the bundler. The same bundler is available from code through Bun.build({ entrypoints, outdir }).
Which bun build flag produces a single standalone executable from your app?
bun build --compile embeds the Bun runtime and your bundled code into one executable file.
Starting with Bun 1.2, what lockfile does bun install create by default?
Bun 1.2 switched the default to the text bun.lock, which is easier to review in diffs. Older versions used the binary bun.lockb.
Which technique is a main reason bun install is fast?
A global cache linked into node_modules
Bun keeps packages in a global cache and links or clones them into node_modules (hardlinks on Linux, clonefile on macOS), avoiding repeated downloads and copies.
Which Bun command adds vitest to devDependencies?
bun add -d (or --dev) records the package under devDependencies. --global installs a package globally instead.
A dependency in a Bun project has a postinstall script, and bun install does not run it. Why?
Bun only runs lifecycle scripts of packages in trustedDependencies
Bun does not support lifecycle scripts at all
postinstall scripts only run on Windows
The script runs later, on first import
For security, Bun skips dependency lifecycle scripts unless the package is listed in trustedDependencies in package.json (a set of popular packages is trusted by default).
What is the Bun equivalent of npx for running a package's binary without installing it?
bunx (an alias of bun x) runs a package's executable, fetching it into the cache if needed.
An existing Express app on Node.js uses node:fs and node:path. What usually happens when you start it with bun index.js?
It runs, since Bun implements most Node.js APIs
It fails, since Bun has no node: modules
It runs only after converting to Bun.serve
It runs only if the code is rewritten in TypeScript
Bun aims to be a drop-in replacement for Node.js and implements most built-in modules and globals such as process and Buffer; some APIs are still incomplete.
A Bun project has a .env file with API_KEY=123 and no dotenv package. What is process.env.API_KEY when you run bun index.ts?
An error about a missing dotenv package
Bun loads .env files automatically (along with variants like .env.local), so dotenv is not needed. Values are also available on Bun.env.
In Bun, what does const f = Bun.file('data.txt'); do before you await f.text()?
Creates a lazy reference; nothing is read yet
Reads the whole file into memory
Throws if the file is larger than 1 MB
Bun.file returns a BunFile that reads lazily. Data is loaded only when you call methods such as text(), json() or arrayBuffer().
Which import gives you Bun's built-in SQLite driver?
bun:sqlite is a native, synchronous SQLite driver that ships with Bun; no npm package is needed.
With bun:sqlite, how do you create a temporary database that lives only in memory?
':memory:' is the standard SQLite name for an in-memory database, which disappears when the connection closes.
With bun:sqlite, which code safely looks up a user by an id that came from user input?
db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ' + id).get()
db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ' + String(id)).get()
db.run('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ' + id)
Bound parameters (?) are sent separately from the SQL text, which prevents SQL injection. String concatenation lets user input change the query.
With bun:sqlite, what does db.query('SELECT name FROM users').all() return?
bun:sqlite is synchronous. all() returns every row as a plain object, get() returns the first row, and run() executes without returning rows.
graphql: In GraphQL SDL, what does the ! in name: String! mean?
The field can never be null
The field is required as an argument
The field is deprecated
The field is a list
! marks a type as non-null. A resolver returning null for it is an error.
A GraphQL field is declared as tags: [String!]. Which value is NOT valid for it?
["a", null]
null
The list itself is nullable, so null and [] are fine, but each item is String!, so a null element is invalid.
Which three root operation types can a GraphQL schema define?
Query, Mutation, Subscription
Get, Post, Delete
Read, Write, Stream
Query, Command, Event
Query is required. Mutation and Subscription are optional root types for writes and real-time events.
What problem does GraphQL address by letting the client choose exactly which fields to fetch?
Over-fetching and under-fetching data
Slow database indexes
Lack of HTTPS support
Missing database transactions in the API layer
Clients ask only for the fields they need, often in one request, instead of calling several fixed REST endpoints.
Which GraphQL operation correctly declares and uses a variable for a user id?
query GetUser($id: ID!) { user(id: $id) { name } }
query GetUser { user(id: $id: ID!) { name } }
query GetUser(id: ID!) { user(id) { name } }
query GetUser($id) { user(id: ID!) { name } }
Variables are declared with $name and a type after the operation name, then referenced as $name in arguments.
In a single GraphQL query you need user(id: 1) and user(id: 2). Which feature avoids a field name conflict?
Aliases, like a: user(id: 1) and b: user(id: 2)
Fragments, like ...UserFields on both fields
Directives, like @include
Variables, like $id1 and $id2 for each field
Two selections of the same field with different arguments conflict. Aliases give each result its own key in the response.
What is a GraphQL fragment used for?
Reusing a set of fields across several queries
Splitting a large response into pages
Running part of a query on the server ahead of time
Caching a query result in the client
A fragment such as fragment UserFields on User { id name } can be spread with ...UserFields wherever that selection is needed.
A GraphQL mutation contains two top-level fields: createUser and addRole. How does the server execute them?
Serially, in the order they appear
In parallel, in any order
Only the first field is executed
In alphabetical order of field names
The GraphQL spec requires top-level mutation fields to run one after another, while query fields may be resolved in parallel.
In GraphQL SDL, which keyword defines a type that can be used as an argument, such as createUser(data: NewUser!)?
input
type
argument
interface
Arguments accept scalars, enums and input object types. Regular object types defined with type cannot be used as input.
How are GraphQL subscriptions most commonly delivered to clients?
Over a long-lived connection such as a WebSocket
Through repeated GET requests every second
Through email notifications
Inside the response headers of a mutation
Subscriptions push events as they happen, usually over WebSockets (for example the graphql-ws protocol) or server-sent events.
In GraphQL.js-style servers (such as Apollo Server), what are the four arguments of a resolver function?
(parent, args, context, info)
(req, res, next, err)
(query, variables, schema, root)
(args, parent, info, context)
parent is the result of the parent field, args are the field arguments, context is shared per request, and info holds execution details.
In a GraphQL server, where should you put the authenticated user and database connection so every resolver can use them?
The context object
The info argument
The root type definition
A global variable in the schema file
The context is created once per request and passed to every resolver, which makes it the right place for per-request data like the current user.
A resolver for a non-null field (email: String!) returns null. What happens in the GraphQL response?
The field errors and null bubbles up to the nearest nullable parent
The field is returned as an empty string with a warning
The whole HTTP request fails with status 500 and no data at all
The field is silently left out
A null in a non-null position is a field error; the null propagates upward until it reaches a field that is allowed to be null.
In GraphQL.js, a field has no resolver defined. What does the default resolver do?
Returns parent[fieldName] from the parent object
Returns null for every value
Throws an error at startup
Queries the database table that has the same name as the field
The default resolver reads parent[fieldName], calling it if it is a function. That is why simple fields often need no resolver.
A GraphQL query fetches 50 posts, and each post's author resolver runs its own SQL query. How many queries hit the database?
One query loads the posts and 50 more load authors one by one. This is the N+1 problem, typically fixed with batching.
How does DataLoader solve the N+1 problem in GraphQL?
It batches loads from one tick into a single request
It caches every query result in the browser
It rewrites nested resolvers into SQL joins automatically
It runs each resolver on its own thread
Calls to loader.load(id) made during the same tick are collected and passed together to one batch function, which can run a single WHERE id IN (...) query.
Why should a GraphQL server create a new DataLoader instance for every request?
Its cache could otherwise leak data between users
DataLoader instances can only be used once and then expire
Batching only works on the first request
A shared instance blocks the event loop
DataLoader memoizes results. A per-request instance prevents one user from seeing another's cached, permission-checked data.
A DataLoader batch function receives the keys [3, 1, 2]. What must it return?
Values for 3, 1 and 2 in that exact order
Values sorted by key: 1, 2, 3
Only the values that were found
A map from each key to its value, in any order
The returned array must have the same length and order as the keys (or a Promise of one), using null or an Error for missing items.
In GraphQL, Pet is an interface implemented by Dog, and only Dog has barkVolume. How do you request barkVolume in a pets query?
pets { name ... on Dog { barkVolume } }
pets { name barkVolume }
pets(type: Dog) { barkVolume }
pets { name Dog.barkVolume }
Fields not declared on the interface must be selected with an inline fragment on the concrete type.
What is the key difference between a GraphQL union and an interface?
Union members do not need to share any fields
Unions can only contain scalar types
Interfaces cannot be returned directly from query fields
Unions can be used as input arguments
An interface defines fields that each implementing type must have. A union just lists object types, so you need fragments for every field except __typename.
rest-apis: Which HTTP method is defined as safe, meaning it should not change server state?
GET
PUT
DELETE
PATCH
Safe methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) are read-only by contract. PUT and DELETE are idempotent but not safe.
Which of these HTTP methods is NOT idempotent by definition?
POST
PUT
DELETE
GET
Repeating a POST may create a new resource each time. Repeating PUT or DELETE leaves the server in the same state as doing it once.
A client wants to change only the email of user 7, sending { "email": "a@b.kz" }. Which method fits a REST API best?
PATCH /users/7
PUT /users/7
POST /users/7/email/update
GET /users/7?email=a@b.kz
PATCH applies a partial update. PUT replaces the whole resource, so fields missing from the body would be lost or reset.
A client sends DELETE /orders/5 twice. The first returns 204, the second returns 404. Is DELETE still idempotent here?
Yes, because the server state is the same after both
No, because the responses differ
No, DELETE is never idempotent
Only if the server returns 204 for both of the requests
Idempotency is about the effect on server state, not identical responses. After either request the order does not exist.
A POST /articles request successfully creates a new article. What is the most appropriate response?
201 Created with a Location header
200 OK with no body
202 Accepted with a Retry-After header
204 No Content with a Location header
201 signals that a new resource was created, and the Location header points to its URI. 202 means processing has not finished yet.
A DELETE request succeeds and the server has nothing to return in the body. Which status code fits?
204 No Content
200 OK with a null body
205 Reset Content
304 Not Modified
204 means success with an intentionally empty body. 304 is for conditional GET requests answered from cache.
A user is logged in but requests an admin-only endpoint. Which status code should a REST API return?
403 Forbidden
401 Unauthorized
404 Not Found
400 Bad Request
401 means credentials are missing or invalid. 403 means the server knows who the user is but refuses access.
A client sends too many requests and hits the API's rate limit. Which status code fits?
429 Too Many Requests
403 Forbidden
503 Service Unavailable
409 Conflict
429 is defined for rate limiting and is often sent with a Retry-After header telling the client when to try again.
A client sends DELETE /products, but the API only supports GET and POST on that URI. Which status code fits?
405 Method Not Allowed
404 Not Found
400 Bad Request
501 Not Implemented
405 means the resource exists but does not support this method; the response must include an Allow header listing supported methods.
Which URI best follows resource-oriented REST design for listing the orders of user 42?
GET /users/42/orders
GET /getUserOrders?id=42
POST /users/42/getOrders
GET /user-orders-list/42
REST URIs name resources with plural nouns and use the HTTP method as the verb. Verbs like get in the path duplicate the method.
In a REST API, how should a client request only the products in the books category?
GET /products?category=books
GET /products/filter/books/category
POST /products/search-books
GET /getProductsByCategory/books
Filtering, sorting and pagination are conventionally expressed as query parameters on the collection URI.
A payment POST may be retried after a network timeout. Which technique prevents charging the customer twice?
Send an idempotency key with each logical request
Switch the endpoint from POST to GET so it is cached
Return 500 for every duplicate attempt
Retry the request with a new random URI
The server stores the result per idempotency key (often an Idempotency-Key header) and returns the same result for a retry instead of processing it again.
What does HATEOAS add to a REST API response?
Links to related resources and possible next actions
A schema describing every database table
A digital signature attached to each response body
Compressed binary encoding of the body
With HATEOAS the client discovers what it can do next (for example cancel or pay links) from hypermedia in the response instead of hard-coding URIs.
Why must you not put a user's password inside a standard signed JWT (JWS) payload?
The payload is only base64url-encoded, so it is readable
The signature becomes invalid whenever the password changes
JWT payloads cannot store string values
The payload is deleted after the first request
A signed JWT protects integrity, not confidentiality. Anyone holding the token can decode the payload, so it must contain no secrets.
A REST API verifies JWTs. Which check is essential to prevent forged tokens?
Verify the signature with a fixed algorithm and reject 'none'
Check that the token has three dot-separated parts
Decode the payload and check that it is valid, well-formed JSON
Check that the token is shorter than 8 KB
Only signature verification with a fixed, expected algorithm proves the token was issued by you; accepting alg 'none' lets attackers craft unsigned tokens.
Which OAuth 2.0 flow is recommended for a single-page app or mobile app that cannot keep a client secret?
Authorization Code flow with PKCE
Implicit flow
Resource Owner Password Credentials flow
Client Credentials flow
Current OAuth security guidance recommends the Authorization Code flow with PKCE for public clients. The implicit flow is deprecated.
Why do APIs commonly issue a short-lived access token together with a longer-lived refresh token?
To limit damage if an access token leaks, without frequent logins
Because access tokens cannot contain user IDs
So the server can skip verifying access tokens on every request
Because refresh tokens are sent with every request
A leaked access token expires quickly. The refresh token, stored more carefully and sent only to the token endpoint, gets new access tokens.
How is an OAuth 2.0 access token usually sent to a REST API?
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-Token: <token> in the body
As a ?password= query parameter
Cookie: bearer=<token> only
The Bearer scheme in the Authorization header is the standard defined by RFC 6750. Tokens in URLs leak into logs and browser history.
Which standard defines a JSON format (media type application/problem+json) for HTTP API error responses?
Problem Details for HTTP APIs (RFC 9457)
JSON:API Errors (RFC 7231)
OpenAPI Error Objects (RFC 6749)
JSON Schema Faults (RFC 8259)
RFC 9457, which obsoletes RFC 7807, defines fields like type, title, status, detail and instance for machine-readable errors.
A REST API hits an unexpected database exception. What should the error response contain?
A 500 status and a generic, consistent error body
A 200 status with error: true and the exception message in the body
A 400 status with the full stack trace
A 404 status with the SQL query
Server faults are 5xx. Clients get a stable error format, while stack traces and SQL stay in server logs to avoid leaking internals.
grpc: What must the first non-comment line of a proto3 file be?
syntax = "proto3";
version = 3;
#proto3
package proto3;
Without the syntax declaration, protoc assumes proto2. The line must come before any other statements.
In proto3, a client never sets the int32 field count. What value does the receiver read?
null
An exception is thrown
proto3 scalar fields have default values: 0 for numbers, empty string for strings, false for bools. Unset and zero look the same on the wire.
In proto3, you need to distinguish an unset int32 field from one explicitly set to 0. What can you use?
Mark it optional, or use a wrapper type
Use the required keyword
Give it field number 0
Declare it as repeated int32
proto3 optional fields (and wrappers like google.protobuf.Int32Value) track presence. required does not exist in proto3.
You delete field 4 (old_email) from a proto3 message. What should you do to keep future versions safe?
Add reserved 4; so the number is never reused
Renumber the remaining fields to close the gap
Reuse number 4 for the next new field
Nothing, numbers are only comments
Field numbers identify fields on the wire. Reusing one could make old data decode into the wrong field, so reserve removed numbers (and names).
In a proto3 message, why are field numbers 1 to 15 usually given to frequently used fields?
They encode in one byte on the wire
They are the only numbers allowed for strings
They are sent compressed with gzip
They are validated faster by protoc
The field number and wire type share a varint tag; numbers 1 to 15 fit in one byte, while 16 to 2047 need two.
What rule applies to the first value of an enum in proto3?
It must have the number 0
It must be named UNKNOWN
It must be the largest number
It cannot be used in messages
The zero value is the default for unset enum fields, so proto3 requires it. Naming it something like STATUS_UNSPECIFIED is a common convention.
Which proto3 declaration defines a simple unary RPC?
rpc GetUser (GetUserRequest) returns (User);
rpc GetUser returns User;
service GetUser (GetUserRequest) -> User;
rpc GetUser (stream GetUserRequest);
RPC methods are declared inside a service block with one request message type and one response message type.
Which proto3 signature describes server streaming: one request, many responses?
rpc List (Filter) returns (stream Item);
rpc List (stream Filter) returns (Item);
rpc List (stream Filter) returns (stream Item);
rpc List (Filter) returns (repeated Item);
The stream keyword on the response side means the server sends a sequence of messages. repeated is for message fields, not RPC signatures.
A client uploads a large file to a gRPC service in chunks and receives one summary at the end. Which RPC type fits?
Client streaming
Unary
Server streaming
Bidirectional streaming
In client streaming the client sends a stream of messages and the server replies once after reading them.
A gRPC chat service lets both sides send messages at any time over one call. Which RPC type fits?
Bidirectional streaming
Client streaming
Server streaming
Unary with polling
With bidirectional streaming both client and server write independent message streams over the same call.
Which HTTP/2 feature lets many concurrent gRPC calls share a single TCP connection?
Multiplexing of streams
Chunked transfer encoding
Keep-alive pipelining
Server push of resources
HTTP/2 multiplexes independent streams over one connection, so calls do not wait for each other like HTTP/1.1 requests.
Why can a browser not call a standard gRPC server directly with fetch?
Browsers do not expose the HTTP/2 control gRPC needs, like trailers
Browsers cannot send binary data
gRPC only works over UDP
Browsers block all HTTP/2 traffic
gRPC relies on HTTP/2 trailers and framing that browser APIs do not expose. gRPC-Web with a proxy such as Envoy fills the gap.
Where does a gRPC server send the final status code (grpc-status) of a call?
In HTTP/2 trailers after the messages
In the HTTP status line only
Inside the first response message
In a separate UDP packet
The HTTP status is usually 200; the gRPC outcome travels as grpc-status and grpc-message in trailers, which is why trailers are required.
A gRPC client sets a 2 second deadline, but the server needs 5 seconds. Which status does the client get?
DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
UNAVAILABLE
CANCELLED
RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
When the deadline passes, the call is terminated on the client with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, and the server can see that the call was cancelled.
How does a gRPC client usually send an auth token with each call?
As call metadata, like an authorization key
As an extra field in every proto message
As a query string on the service URL
Inside the .proto file as an option
Metadata is a key-value map carried as HTTP/2 headers, which keeps cross-cutting data like tokens out of the message schema.
You add a new field to a proto3 message, and an old client that does not know it receives the message. What happens?
The old client ignores the unknown field
The old client fails to decode the message
The server refuses to send the message
The new field replaces field number 1
Adding fields with new numbers is backward compatible; parsers skip or keep unknown fields, which is why protobuf schemas can evolve.
Which tool compiles .proto files into language-specific code such as Go or Java classes?
protoc
grpcurl
buf curl
protolint
protoc is the Protocol Buffers compiler; plugins (such as protoc-gen-go-grpc) add gRPC client and server code. grpcurl only calls services.
In gRPC terminology, what is the generated client-side object that exposes service methods called?
A stub
A skeleton
A proxy table
A servlet
Generated stubs have one method per RPC; calling one serializes the request and sends it to the server.
Which Node.js package loads .proto files at runtime so you can use gRPC without a code generation step?
@grpc/proto-loader
@grpc/protoc-gen
grpc-tools-runtime
@protobuf/loader-cli
@grpc/proto-loader parses .proto files dynamically, and @grpc/grpc-js uses the result to build clients and servers.
Why are gRPC messages usually smaller than equivalent JSON payloads?
Protobuf is binary and uses field numbers, not names
gRPC always gzips every message
Protobuf drops fields that are not strings
HTTP/2 removes duplicate values from bodies
Protobuf encodes compact varints and field tags instead of repeating text keys, which shrinks payloads and speeds up parsing.
websockets: What does it mean that a WebSocket connection is full-duplex?
Both sides can send messages independently at the same time
Only the server can send after the handshake
The client must wait for a reply before sending again
Each message opens a new TCP connection to the server
After the handshake, client and server share one TCP connection and either side can send frames at any moment.
How does a browser open a WebSocket connection to a server?
An HTTP GET with Upgrade: websocket headers
A POST with Content-Type: websocket
A raw UDP packet to port 80
A DNS lookup with a WS record
The client sends an HTTP/1.1 GET with Upgrade: websocket and Connection: Upgrade, plus a Sec-WebSocket-Key header.
What status code does a server return to accept a WebSocket upgrade request?
101 Switching Protocols
200 OK
201 Created
426 Upgrade Required
101 confirms the protocol switch, after which the connection speaks WebSocket framing instead of HTTP.
What is the purpose of the Sec-WebSocket-Key and Sec-WebSocket-Accept headers in the handshake?
To prove the server understood the handshake
To encrypt every message that follows the handshake
To authenticate the user
To choose a compression algorithm
The server hashes the key with a fixed GUID (SHA-1, then base64). It is not a security mechanism; TLS (wss://) provides encryption.
Which URL should a page served over HTTPS use for its WebSocket connection?
wss://example.com/socket
ws://example.com/socket
https://example.com/socket?ws
socket://example.com
wss:// runs WebSocket over TLS. Browsers block insecure ws:// connections from HTTPS pages as mixed content.
In the browser, const ws = new WebSocket(url); ws.send('hi'); runs immediately. What happens?
send() throws, as the socket is still connecting
The message is queued until the socket opens
The message is sent over HTTP instead
The browser silently drops the message
While readyState is CONNECTING, send() throws an InvalidStateError. Send inside the open event handler or after checking readyState.
What does readyState === 1 mean on a browser WebSocket object?
OPEN
CONNECTING
CLOSING
CLOSED
The values are 0 CONNECTING, 1 OPEN, 2 CLOSING and 3 CLOSED. Messages can be sent only when it is OPEN.
Which WebSocket frame opcode carries a ping control frame?
0x1 is text, 0x2 is binary, 0x8 is close, 0x9 is ping and 0xA is pong.
In the WebSocket protocol, which frames must be masked?
Frames sent from client to server
Frames sent from server to client
Only control frames
Only binary frames
Clients must mask every frame, and servers must not. Masking prevents cache poisoning attacks on intermediaries that misread the traffic.
How does the WebSocket protocol mark the last frame of a fragmented message?
The FIN bit is set to 1
The opcode is set to 0x0
The payload ends with a null byte
The mask key is set to zero
Fragments after the first use the continuation opcode 0x0, and the FIN bit is set only on the final fragment.
What limits apply to WebSocket control frames such as ping and close?
Payload of 125 bytes at most, never fragmented
Payload of 64 KB at most, may be fragmented
No payload is allowed at all in control frames
They must be sent only by the server
RFC 6455 limits control frame payloads to 125 bytes and forbids fragmenting them, so they can be injected between fragments of a data message.
Browser JavaScript needs to detect that its WebSocket connection silently died. Why do apps send their own heartbeat messages?
The browser API cannot send protocol ping frames
Ping frames are not part of the protocol
Browsers close idle sockets after 1 second
Heartbeats encrypt the connection
Browsers answer server pings automatically but expose no ping() method, so client-side liveness checks use small application messages.
What is a main reason servers send periodic WebSocket pings to clients?
To detect dead connections and keep proxies open
To measure the client's CPU speed and network latency
To renew the TLS certificate before it expires
To reset the message counter
A connection can be half-open with no error. Missing pongs reveal it, and regular traffic stops load balancers from closing idle connections.
Thousands of clients lose their WebSocket connection when a server restarts. Which reconnect strategy is best?
Exponential backoff with random jitter
Reconnect immediately in a tight loop
Reconnect at the same fixed interval
Never reconnect; ask users to reload
Backoff with jitter spreads reconnects over time and avoids a thundering herd that could overload the server as it comes back.
A browser WebSocket fires the close event with code 1006. What does that mean?
It closed abnormally, without a close frame
The server closed it normally
The client sent invalid UTF-8
The message was too big for the server to process
1006 is reserved for when the connection drops without a closing handshake; it is never sent in a frame. 1000 is normal closure, 1009 is message too big.
In Socket.IO, which code sends a message to every client in the room game1, including the sender?
io.to('game1').emit('move', data)
socket.to('game1').emit('move', data)
socket.broadcast.emit('move', data)
socket.emit('game1', 'move', data)
io.to(room) targets all sockets in the room. socket.to(room) and socket.broadcast exclude the sending socket.
In Socket.IO, what does socket.broadcast.emit('joined', name) do?
Sends to all connected clients except the sender
Sends only to the sender, as a confirmation
Sends to all clients including the sender
Sends to clients in the sender's rooms only
broadcast excludes the current socket. Combine with to(room) to limit it to a room.
A Socket.IO app runs on three server instances, and room broadcasts only reach clients on the same instance. What fixes it?
An adapter such as the Redis adapter
Increasing the ping interval on every instance
Switching to long-polling only
Using one room per server
Each instance only knows its own sockets. An adapter (Redis, Postgres and others) relays broadcasts between instances via pub/sub.
Can a plain browser WebSocket client connect directly to a Socket.IO server and exchange events?
No, Socket.IO adds its own protocol on top
Yes, Socket.IO is plain WebSocket under another name
Yes, but only for text messages
Only if the server uses wss://
Socket.IO has its own packet format, handshake and fallbacks, so it needs a Socket.IO client library on the other side.
The browser WebSocket API cannot set custom headers such as Authorization. How is a WebSocket usually authenticated?
With a cookie, a short-lived URL token, or a first auth message
By passing an Authorization header in the WebSocket constructor
By sending the password in every frame
They cannot, so WebSocket endpoints must stay public
Common options are session cookies (with an Origin check), a short-lived ticket in the query string, or an auth message right after connecting.
